When you see a donate button on a video game mod that you play frequently for example, and do not click it, why is that?

This is not trying to guilt people in any way into donating more. I'm genuinely curious about people's feelings and thoughts when they choose not to donate to something that they value because I want to try and design a better donation system. Patreon exists, which is great, though it isn't exactly a pure donation system. Flattr is pretty interesting too, but it isn't widespread either. I'd like to understand what can be done to help people feel comfortable returning some of the value they've derived from the free gifts of others without requiring that folks enter into a traditional commercial arrangement that can stifle some of the beauty and innovation that comes with the labors of love.

(Interestingly when i tried to ask this on /r/askreddit a short while ago it was instantly removed with the claim that it violated their first two rules - even though it didn't. I think that the reason that it's free to begin with is a big part of why you'd be using it. For example I don't really like using Gimp much over Photoshop but it now costs $90 for the privilege of renting that app for a year. A right kick in the guts when you consider that Adobe haven't bothered to do anything innovative with it for decades and simply rest on the fact that they're the current industry standard.

Or in other words saying that you're obligated to donate to something kind of misses the point of an app being free to begin with, IMHO. If you wanted to use payware then you wouldn't be seeking out the free application to begin with. Granted some of these projects are equivalent or better than paid services, but the majority of the time this simply isn't the case.

It's a catch-22 situation now that I think about it.

If I could, somehow, monetize my comments, submissions, and contributions to Voat, I would be more likely to aggregate content and spend way more time than I do now on Voat to give back to this platform and donate. As it stand right now, that system is currently closed for new applicants and if that is the case. the only other way I am going to donate to this platform or any other platform is when I retire, am able to physically volunteer for that organization, or have a more secure employment situation. Not everyone who can donate does and not everyone who can't donate is unwilling.

We see social contributions starting to be rewarded on reddit through things like bitcoin tips. I hope it's the baby-steps of a new economy, with that sort of thing. We do see it. The internet occasionally decides a random person is deserving of more than they have, and the donations roll in. People are good, for the most part, it's how we survive as communities. We want to help each other, but there are a lot of barriers in the way.

I do what I can. If I hear some music I really like on bandcamp and it's pay-what-you-want, I will throw a few bucks their way. A few times I donated to the authors of Android apps I really liked. However, I'm a student with a part-time job and I need every bit of money that I earn. I hardly ever donate other than the above cases, because I simply can't justify spending the money.
